aesthetic: Papier Suisse — a warm-ground Swiss grid system that moves from amber morning light to cool evening blue across 44 slides, speaking entirely through alignment, measure, and a single migrating accent bar
chromaticArc: Slides 1–14 carry Morning Amber accent bars on a Warm White ground; slides 15–28 transition through Slate Horizon as the ground shifts subtly to Cool White; slides 29–44 settle into Evening Blue accents, with the three chapter-break slides (roughly 11, 23, 37) using Warm Linen as a mid-tone bg to mark the arc's seams without ever going dark
gridStrategy: The accent bar's column position increments by +3 cols every ~11 slides — opening at col 4, advancing to col 7, then col 10, then col 13 — so the bar drifts rightward across the deck as a spatial echo of the warm-to-cool gradient, while title and body zones hold their left anchor at col 4–6 throughout, making the bar the sole dynamic element in the grid

fontStrategy.secondarySlides: No secondary font is used; all typographic hierarchy is achieved through size, tracking (0.12em on labels, 0.02em on body), and spatial separation within Helvetica Neue alone

accentStrategy: Each slide carries a single 2-col-wide × 5-row-tall coloured bar whose column position advances rightward in four stages (cols 4, 7, 10, 13) and whose colour is drawn from the current arc phase — Morning Amber on slides 1–14, Aged Gold on transitional slides, Slate Horizon mid-deck, Evening Blue on slides 29–44 — so the bar functions simultaneously as a page anchor, a progress index, and the deck's only decorative element
